subject: Residency control-plane HA: EU/APAC failover acceptance and test plan
messages:
From: Maria Olsen <maria.olsen@nordicbank.dk>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Saito Tanaka <saito@jp-consulting.co.jp>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Residency acceptance criteria for EU primary / APAC DR private deploy

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement checklist, our security team needs a short, testable acceptance matrix for the control-plane and data residency behavior when an EU-hosted private deployment (VPC) needs to fail over to an APAC warm-standby.

High level asks:
- Confirm where customer metadata and audit logs persist during a failover (EU-only vs replicated).
- Expected RTO/RPO for control-plane and inference traffic for Dedicated vs Private (VPC) installs.
- Network authorization expectations (required peering/AWS Transit / static routes) and whether Redwood will provide config snippets.
- Any data movement (encrypted snapshots, logs) that crosses EU borders during warm failover and what controls are available (encryption, keys, retention).

We want these as acceptance criteria we can sign off after a joint runbook exercise. Attached is a template residency-acceptance-criteria.xlsx — can you propose edits and call out what Redwood can guarantee vs recommended customer config?

Thanks,
Maria
Head of Cloud Risk — NordicBank

[attachment: residency-acceptance-criteria.xlsx]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Olsen <maria.olsen@nordicbank.dk>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 10:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Residency acceptance criteria for EU primary / APAC DR private deploy

Maria —

Appreciate the clear template. I ran this by Markus (infra lead) and Priyom (security) and sketched a concise acceptance matrix and a proposed runbook for a joint tabletop + live failover test. Key items below — I'll attach our initial draft runbook and a network topology diagram.

Summary (short answers):
- Audit logs and customer metadata: retained in EU by default; we support encrypted, one-way replication of minimal operational metadata to APAC for failover only (configurable).
- RTO/RPO: Private (VPC): RTO target 15m for control-plane, RPO 5m for KV/cache metadata when replication enabled. Dedicated pool (reserved) slightly better depending on reserved hotspots — we can commit to 10m/1m under contract.
- Network: we provide BGP peering reference and Transit examples; customer must expose static eBGP or use AWS Transit Gateway/Cloud Router with the provided CIDR mappings.
- Cross-border snapshots: snapshots can be configured to remain in-region; however, application-level ephemeral state will be streamed to APAC during warm failover unless customer disables replication. All transfers use customer KMS or Redwood-managed CMKs if requested.

Next steps:
1) Markus/Laur a + Priyom to convert the template into acceptance rows and mark which items Redwood will sign off on vs customer responsibility.
2) Schedule a 2hr tabletop with NordicBank + JP consulting and then a live runbook window (2hrs) to exercise actual failover.
3) Share network config snippets and a DocuSign acceptance checklist for final sign-off.

I'll follow up with the marked spreadsheet by Monday and propose times for the tabletop.

— Vanessa
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Maria Olsen <maria.olsen@nordicbank.dk>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 11:40:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Residency acceptance criteria for EU primary / APAC DR private deploy

Vanessa / Maria —

Quick technical clarifications to include in the acceptance rows (I edited the attached sheet):
- Control-plane: our control-plane state is multi-tenant metadata (deployments, routes, keys). For Private (customer-managed VPC) the control-plane is logically isolated; we run a lightweight control-plane agent inside customer VPC and the master control-plane node remains in the customer's preferred region unless replication is enabled.
- Replication modes:
  * None: no data leaves EU; manual failover required (longer RTO).
  * Minimal (recommended): replicate only metadata and audit-index to APAC; full model artifacts remain EU-only and are pulled on demand (adds ~3–7 minutes per model load).
  * Full (customer opt-in): encrypted snapshot replication for artifacts and model shards. This is the only mode that will incur cross-border artifact movement pre-failover.
- Test signal and verification: we'll provide a signed test token and an endpoint checklist to validate post-failover routing and token issuance.

I've tagged rows where Redwood is the owner. Priyom, please flag anything that needs policy language.

— Markus
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Maria Olsen <maria.olsen@nordicbank.dk>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 13:22:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Residency acceptance criteria for EU primary / APAC DR private deploy

Thanks — a few security/risk notes to insert into the acceptance checklist before client sign-off:
- Key ownership: clarify whether NordicBank requires customer-managed KMS (we recommend) vs Redwood-managed CMK. Acceptance must list which operations require KMS access during failover (snapshot decryption, re-encryption).
- Audit trail: we will include immutable audit events with region tags; acceptance must specify retention window and export formats (CSV/JSON) for compliance review.
- Legal hold & e-discovery: if customer requires legal hold, we need a documented retention policy and a runbook step to disable cross-region transfers during legal hold windows.

Attached two suggested acceptance rows and wording for KMS plus a short example clause the customer can add to their procurement security addendum.

— Priyom
Head of Product Security

[attachment: residency-acceptance-criteria.xlsx]

From: Saito Tanaka <saito@jp-consulting.co.jp>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Maria Olsen <maria.olsen@nordicbank.dk>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 18:43:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Residency acceptance criteria for EU primary / APAC DR private deploy

Thanks all — the draft runbook looks good. A few pragmatic asks from the operations side:
- Could Redwood provide terraform snippets or CloudFormation templates for the peering/transit setup? Having copy-paste configs shortens our test window.
- During the live failover test, can Redwood run the reversal (APAC back to EU) as a controlled step? We want a symmetric test to measure time-to-stabilize.
- Please confirm whether any of the default monitoring alerts are adjusted during the test to avoid noisy pages — we prefer a scheduled maintenance window and an alert-suppression toggle on Redwood Console for the host account.

Happy to take the first draft of the acceptance rows and produce a JP-localized checklist for our ops team.

Regards,
Saito
Senior Cloud Architect — JP Consulting
